name: Paro valley farmhouse homestays
price_band: ₹2,500–4,500 per person per night with meals
summary: Certified farmhouse homestays in Paro valley villages such as Shaba, Satsam and Tsento give the cheapest legal stay in Paro and a close look at farm life. Rooms are simple, meals are home-cooked and a hot stone bath is usually on offer.
body: Paro's villages are full of large, traditional farmhouses with painted windows and an altar room upstairs. A number of families are registered with the Department of Tourism to host visitors, which is required for any tourist stay in Bhutan. You sleep in a clean room with thick quilts, share meals with the family and often help in the kitchen.

We book farmhouses that have hot water, an attached or private bathroom and a host who speaks English or Hindi. They sit 5–15 km from Paro town, close to the Taktsang trailhead or Kyichu Lhakhang, so you still need a car. Expect red rice, ema datshi, buckwheat pancakes and local vegetables; ara, the farm spirit, is offered but never expected.
why: The lowest certified price in Paro, with dinner and breakfast included
A real farm family, not a hotel dressed up as one
Hot stone baths after the Taktsang walk
Quiet villages close to Taktsang and Kyichu Lhakhang

faqs.q: Are Paro farmhouse homestays allowed for tourists?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are registered and certified by Bhutan's Department of Tourism. Tourists may stay only in certified accommodation, and your booking is checked during the permit process. We book only registered farmhouses. Do not arrange a stay with an uncertified family, as it can cause permit problems. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What facilities do Paro farmhouses have?
faqs.a: Simple but clean rooms with quilts, usually an attached or private bathroom with hot water, and meals with the family. Wi-Fi may be weak and room heating limited, so winter nights are cold. Bring slippers, a torch and warm layers. Hosts can arrange a hot stone bath for an extra charge.

faqs.q: Is a farmhouse cheaper than a hotel in Paro?
faqs.a: Usually. A farmhouse with dinner and breakfast costs about ₹2,500–4,500 per person, while a three-star hotel room costs ₹6,000–9,000 before meals. The SDF of ₹1,200 per person per night applies either way. For families, a farmhouse often works out cheaper per head.

name: Hotel Druk, Phuentsholing
summary: Hotel Druk is a long-established hotel a short walk from the Bhutan Gate and the immigration office in Phuentsholing. It is a dependable first or last night in Bhutan with air-conditioned rooms and a restaurant serving Bhutanese and Indian food.
body: The hotel stands near the town centre, close to the gate and the Zangtho Pelri temple, which makes it easy to walk to the immigration office early in the morning. Rooms are plain and comfortable, with air conditioning, which matters in Phuentsholing's heat for much of the year.

The restaurant serves Bhutanese, Indian and Chinese dishes, and the staff are used to handling Indian families and groups crossing the border. It belongs to the Druk Hotels group, which also runs Hotel Druk in Thimphu.
why: Walking distance to the immigration office and the gate
Air-conditioned rooms for hot Phuentsholing nights
Reliable restaurant with Indian and Bhutanese food
Certified for tourists, so permits go through smoothly

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Druk from the Phuentsholing immigration office?
faqs.a: A few minutes' walk. The hotel is in the town centre near the Bhutan Gate, so guests can reach the immigration office as soon as it opens. This saves time on the morning you collect permits and leave for Thimphu or Paro. Taxis and buses are also close by.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Druk Phuentsholing have air conditioning?
faqs.a: Yes. Rooms are air-conditioned, which is important from March to October, when Phuentsholing is hot and humid with temperatures often above 30°C. In winter the climate is mild and fans are usually enough. Check current room types when booking.

faqs.q: Is it worth staying in Phuentsholing rather than Jaigaon?
faqs.a: If you value quiet, clean streets and an easy morning at immigration, yes. A night in Phuentsholing does add the SDF of ₹1,200 per person. Budget travellers often sleep in Jaigaon instead. Hotel Druk suits those who want a calm first night in Bhutan.

name: Hotel Druk, Thimphu
summary: Hotel Druk is a central Thimphu hotel on Clock Tower Square, within walking distance of Norzin Lam, cafés and the Memorial Chorten. It is a sound mid-range choice for travellers who want to walk around the city.
body: The hotel overlooks the Clock Tower Square at the heart of the city, with the main shopping street and many restaurants a few minutes away on foot. Rooms are traditionally decorated, heated in winter and comfortable, and the in-house restaurant serves Bhutanese, Indian and continental dishes.

Its location saves taxi fares and lets you explore the city in the evenings without relying on a car. It is run by the Druk Hotels group, which also operates Hotel Druk in Phuentsholing, and is used to Indian families and groups.
why: Central location on Clock Tower Square
Walk to Norzin Lam, cafés and the Memorial Chorten
Heated rooms for winter nights
Experienced with Indian families and groups

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Druk in Thimphu?
faqs.a: On Clock Tower Square in the city centre, a short walk from Norzin Lam, the main street. The Memorial Chorten is about 15 minutes away on foot, and the weekend market about 10 minutes. Tashichho Dzong and the Buddha Dordenma need a short taxi ride.

faqs.q: Are rooms at Hotel Druk Thimphu heated?
faqs.a: Rooms have heating for the cold months from November to March, when Thimphu nights fall below freezing. Confirm the heating type when booking if you are travelling in mid-winter. Summers are mild, and air conditioning is not usually needed in Thimphu.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Druk good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Its central position, restaurant with Indian food, and staff used to families make it an easy base. Interconnecting or extra-bed options may be available on request. Ask for a room away from the square if you are a light sleeper, as the centre can be lively in the evening.

name: Hotel Olathang
summary: Hotel Olathang is one of Bhutan's oldest hotels, set in pine forest on a hillside above Paro and built in the 1970s for guests at the fourth king's coronation. It offers spacious grounds, traditional architecture and valley views at a mid-range price.
body: The hotel sits about 3 km above Paro town among blue pines, with a main building and cottages in traditional style spread across the grounds. It was built to host foreign guests at the coronation of the fourth king in 1974 and has been receiving visitors ever since.

Rooms are comfortable rather than modern, with heating, wooden furnishings and, in many, views over the valley towards Rinpung Dzong. The quiet setting suits travellers who want rest before or after the Taktsang walk. You will need a car to reach town and the trailhead.
why: Historic hotel with traditional Bhutanese architecture
Quiet pine-forest setting with valley views
Mid-range price for spacious grounds
Close to Rinpung Dzong and the National Museum

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Olathang from Paro town?
faqs.a: About 3 km uphill, 10 minutes by car. Rinpung Dzong and the National Museum are close by, while the Taktsang trailhead is about 15 km away, roughly 30 minutes' drive. Walking into town is possible downhill, but most guests use their car or a taxi.

Yes. It is one of the oldest hotels in Bhutan, built in the 1970s to house foreign guests attending the coronation of the fourth king in 1974. It has kept its traditional design, with a main building and cottages set in pine forest above the valley.

Rooms are comfortable and heated but traditional rather than modern, with wooden furnishings. Some guests find the style charming; others prefer newer hotels. Ask for a cottage or valley-view room when booking, and check current room types and rates.

name: Dewachen Hotel, Gangtey
summary: Dewachen is a stone-and-timber hotel on the slope above Phobjikha valley, with heated rooms and views over the crane roosting grounds. It is the best-known mid-to-upper hotel in the valley below the luxury lodges.
body: The hotel is built in traditional style with thick stone walls, wooden floors and large windows facing the valley. Rooms have wood-burning stoves or heaters, which matter on winter nights when the temperature falls well below zero. The dining room serves Bhutanese and continental meals.

It sits a short drive from Gangtey Goenpa and the crane information centre, and the nature trail starts close by. In crane season it fills early, so book well ahead for late October to mid-November and around the 11 November festival.
why: Warm rooms with stoves in a cold valley
Views across the crane roosting marsh
Close to Gangtey Goenpa and the nature trail
Comfort without the cost of the luxury lodges

faqs.q: Can I see cranes from Dewachen Hotel?
faqs.a: The hotel overlooks the valley, and in crane season you can often see and hear the birds in the marsh below, especially at dawn and dusk. For closer views use binoculars or visit the crane information centre a short drive away. The cranes are present from late October to February.

Rooms have wood-burning stoves or heaters, and staff light them in the evening. Phobjikha nights fall to about -5°C in mid-winter, so the stoves make a real difference. Bring warm layers for walking around the valley in the early morning.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I book Dewachen?
faqs.a: For late October to mid-November and the 11 November Crane Festival, book two to three months ahead. In other seasons a few weeks is usually enough. Your tour operator must include the booking with your route permit application. Check current rates before you travel.

name: Le Méridien Thimphu
summary: Le Méridien Thimphu is an international five-star hotel in the city centre near the Wang Chhu and the weekend market. It is the most reliable full-service hotel in the capital for travellers who want the best rooms on the route.
body: The hotel is built in modern Bhutanese style a short walk from Norzin Lam, the Clock Tower Square and the Centenary Farmers Market. Rooms are large, heated and well insulated, with good beds, and there is a spa, a fitness room and several dining options including Indian and Bhutanese food.

It suits honeymooners, older travellers and families who want consistent international standards after long drives. Rates vary with the season and the Tshechu; book early for October and for the Thimphu Tshechu.
why: Central location within walking distance of the market and Norzin Lam
Large, heated rooms with international standards
Spa and good restaurants after long drives
Dependable service for honeymoons and older travellers

faqs.q: Where is Le Méridien in Thimphu?
faqs.a: In the city centre near the Wang Chhu, a short walk from Norzin Lam, the Clock Tower Square and the Centenary Farmers Market. The Memorial Chorten is a few minutes away by car. Tashichho Dzong and the Buddha Dordenma are 10–20 minutes' drive.

faqs.q: Is Le Méridien Thimphu worth the price?
faqs.a: For travellers who want international comfort, yes. Rooms are large and warm, and the spa and restaurants make long driving days easier. Budget travellers will find certified three-star hotels in central Thimphu at a third of the price. The SDF applies at every hotel.

faqs.q: Does Le Méridien Thimphu serve Indian food?
faqs.a: Yes. The restaurants serve Indian dishes along with Bhutanese, Asian and continental food, and vegetarian meals are easy to arrange. Breakfast includes Indian options. Ask the hotel for Jain or other special diets when booking.
